_notes: 10 frames at 200 ms, voice 0.5. Faces of 300 px at x 400 (A, centre 550) and x 800 (B, centre 950), both mouths alternating 0.1/0.3.
Both have lips 1 on every frame and score (0.6 + continuity) / 0.65 > 0.5: an overlap on all 10 frames (2 s >= 1.5 s).
Frame 0: equal scores, no priority, so the lower id, p1, becomes the current speaker; B never beats A by 0.15, so p1 holds the frame on every frame.
Both faces span 400 to 1100 = 700 px, wider than the 608 px window, so a split is tried.

Each region wants max(round(300 / 0.35) = 857, ceil(1080 / 2) = 540) = 857 px, but must keep the other face out: at most 2 * 400 - 300 = 500 px wide, so floor(500 * 1920 / 2160) = 444 px tall. 960 / 444 = 2.16x, over the 200% limit.
A single window is 1080 px tall for 1920: 1.78x, within the limit. So the segment is single on whoever held the frame, p1, reason overlap.
One cut key on A's centre: x 550; y = 300 + 0.38 * 1080 = 710.4, clamped to the only position, 540; h 1080, no layout.
Changed with the sharp-split rule: the old faces (60 px, 900 apart) now get 540 px regions and split, see plan-close-split.
